title: Translations extend near the image of the square-condition section-ring Proj map
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $H\to S$ a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with an $S$-group scheme structure and connected fibres $H_s=H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-connected-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme means a scheme $H$ with $S$-morphisms $m:H\times_SH\to H$, $i:H\to H$, $e:S\to H$ satisfying associativity, identity and inverse identities; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $X\to S$ be a separated morphism of finite presentation, equipped with an action $a:H\times_SX\to X$, meaning that $a(e,x)=x$ and $a(g,a(h,x))=a(gh,x)$ as morphism identities. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For any $S$-scheme $B$, put $X_B=X\times_SB$, with structure map $q_B:X_B\to B$, and let $M_B$ be the tensor pullback of $M$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $g\in H(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,H)$ let $\tau_g:X_B\to X_B$ be the action $x\mapsto gx$. Say that $M$ satisfies the square condition for this action if, for every such $B$ and every $g,h\in H(B)$, there is an invertible $\mathcal O_B$-module $N$ and an isomorphism $$\tau_{gh}^*M_B\otimes M_B\cong\tau_g^*M_B\otimes\tau_h^*M_B\otimes q_B^*N.$$ All tensors are module sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This is equality of the translation differences in the group of invertible-module classes modulo modules pulled back from $B$; no coherence or chosen isomorphisms are part of the condition. Assume that $M$ satisfies this square condition. Assume that the opens $X_s$, over all positive integers $n$ and sections $s\in\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes n})$, cover $X$. Let $$A=\Gamma_*(X,M)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes n})$$ be the graded section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], let $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], and let $r:X\to P$ be the canonical morphism of [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map]. For every affine $S$-scheme $B$ whose structure morphism $B\to S$ is smooth, write $P_B=P\times_SB$ and $r_B=r\times_S\mathrm{id}_B:X_B\to P_B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $g\in H(B)$ there exist open subschemes $U_g,U^{\prime}_g\subseteq P_B$, both containing the image of $r_B$, and a $B$-isomorphism $\sigma_g:U_g\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{\prime}_g$ such that $\sigma_g\circ r_B=r_B\circ\tau_g$, where $r_B$ is factored through the indicated opens. No compatibility between the isomorphisms for different $g$ is asserted.

source.place: Guo, section 5.6 (Picard-admissibility), section 6.1 (flat base change), and Proposition 6.2, first assertion before (i)--(iii), printed pp.14--15, March 31, 2026 version, read online; local copy WANTED. Smooth affine test-base specialization of that assertion, identifying its Proj with the base change of P; proof referred there to Raynaud, Faisceaux amples sur les schemas en groupes et les espaces homogenes, chapitre V, proposition 3.1 and corollaire 3.6.

proof.text: Fix a smooth affine $B\to S$. It is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The finite-presentation hypothesis includes quasi-compactness. By [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change], $q:Y=X_B\to B$ is quasi-compact and separated. Since $B$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Put $R=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ and $T=\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)$. Applying [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] in degree zero to $M^{\otimes n}$ gives $\Gamma(Y,M_B^{\otimes n})=\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes n})\otimes_R T$. The maps send $s\otimes b$ to $b\,s_B$; their product on two pure tensors is $(s\otimes b)(t\otimes c)=st\otimes bc$, so they form a graded $T$-algebra isomorphism. By [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension], $P_B$ identifies with $P_L=\operatorname{Proj}\Gamma_*(Y,L)$ for $L=M_B$. Under this identification $r_B=r_L$: on the pulled-back standard charts both maps have the fraction formula $t/s^k\mapsto t_B/s_B^k$ of [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map]. These charts cover by the scalar-extension node. The original section opens pull back to a cover of $Y$, so $r_L$ is defined everywhere.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero; constructions.tex Tag 01N2, lemma-base-change-map-proj; Guo section 6.1

proof.text: Fix $g\in H(B)$ and write $\tau=\tau_g:Y\to Y$. The action identities give the inverse $\tau_{g^{-1}}$. Put $K=\tau^*L$, $J=\tau_{g^{-1}}^*L$ and $D=\tau_{g^2}^*L$. They are invertible by the local rank-one description [def-sc-invertible-module]. Every translate is covered by its positive-power section opens: pull back the covering for $L$ along the corresponding automorphism. Applying the assumed square identity to $(g,g^{-1})$, and then pulling that identity back by $\tau$, using that $\tau^*$ carries tensor products to tensor products [lem-pc-scheme-pullback-monoidal-existing], gives invertible modules $N_0,N_1$ on $B$ and isomorphisms $L^{\otimes2}\cong K\otimes J\otimes q^*N_0$ and $K^{\otimes2}\cong D\otimes L\otimes q^*N_1$. In the second formula use $\tau_{g^{-1}}\circ\tau_g=\mathrm{id}$, $\tau_g\circ\tau_g=\tau_{g^2}$ and $q\tau=q$.

source.place: Section 5.6 and Corollary 5.8; direct substitution in the assumed square condition

proof.text: Let $t\in\Gamma(Y,K^{\otimes n})$, $n>0$, and $y\in Y_t$. Since positive-power section opens for $J$ cover, choose $m>0$ and $u\in\Gamma(Y,J^{\otimes m})$ nonzero at $y$. The first identity of Step 2 identifies $t^{\otimes m}\otimes u^{\otimes n}\otimes q^*v$ with a section $s$ of $L^{\otimes2nm}$, for any $v\in\Gamma(B,N_0^{\otimes nm})$. The module $N_0^{\otimes nm}$ is invertible and thus quasi-coherent of finite type; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections] gives a global generator family. At $q(y)$ some member $v$ has nonzero residue. Then $s(y)\ne0$ and $Y_s\subseteq Y_t$. Indeed, in a local frame $s$ has coefficient $a^m b^n c$, where $a,b,c$ are the coefficients of $t,u,q^*v$. A product in the residue field is nonzero exactly when every factor is nonzero. Thus each $K$-section open is refined at every point by an $L$-section open.

source.place: Agent argument from Corollary 5.8; affine generation: Stacks properties.tex Tag 01PB, lemma-finite-type-module

proof.text: Conversely, let $s\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes d})$, $d>0$, and $y\in Y_s$. Choose $e>0$ and $u\in\Gamma(Y,D^{\otimes e})$ nonzero at $y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections] on the affine $B$ to $N_1^{\otimes de}$ and choose a global section $v$ nonzero at $q(y)$. The second identity of Step 2 carries $u^{\otimes d}\otimes s^{\otimes e}\otimes q^*v$ to $t\in\Gamma(Y,K^{\otimes2de})$. Its residue at $y$ is nonzero and $Y_t\subseteq Y_s$, since its local coefficient is the product of those of $u^d,s^e,q^*v$. This proves the other refinement condition. No base twist was assumed globally trivial.

source.place: Agent argument from Corollary 5.8, applied after translation; affine generation as in Step 3

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cofinal-section-opens-proj-neighborhood] to $Y/B,L,K$, with the two covers of Step 2 and the refinements of Steps 3--4. It gives $\theta:V_L\simeq V_K$ with $\theta r_L=r_K$. Pullback along $\tau$ gives a graded $T$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha:\Gamma_*(Y,L)\simeq\Gamma_*(Y,K)$: on each degree it is pullback of sections, inverse to pullback by $\tau^{-1}$ with the canonical line identifications, and it preserves multiplication of tensor sections. By [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] it induces $F:P_K\simeq P_L$. Concretely, [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] applied to both rings equal to $T$ with the identity map, the graded rings $\Gamma_*(Y,L)$, $\Gamma_*(Y,K)$ and the graded isomorphism $\alpha$ (after $T\otimes_T\Gamma_*(Y,L)=\Gamma_*(Y,L)$) gives $F$ as the morphism cartesian over $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_T)$, with $F^{-1}(D_+(s))=D_+(\tau^*s)$ and the chart ring map $t/s^k\mapsto\tau^*t/(\tau^*s)^k$. The canonical-map formula [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map] gives $F r_K=r_L\tau$: over $D_+(s)$ both composites are defined on $r_K^{-1}D_+(\tau^*s)=\tau^{-1}(Y_s)$ and induce $t/s^k\mapsto\tau^*t/(\tau^*s)^k=\tau^*(t/s^k)$ on global sections, and $D_+(s)$ is affine. Set $U_g=V_L$, $U'_g=F(V_K)$ and $\sigma_g=F\theta$, transported through $P_L=P_B$ from Step 1. Both opens contain $r_B(Y)$, since $F(r_K(Y))=r_L(\tau(Y))=r_L(Y)$. Finally $\sigma_g r_B=F r_K=r_B\tau_g$, as required.
